What happens if you remove the second condition here? I would have assumed that walking up `window.parent` should lead you to the top frame without any other conditions. It may not be the actual top window. In fact, it's only the top window when we open the snapshot in a new tab. In trace viewer / UI mode, it must be the snapshot root window, which is an iframe:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/864dc96f-06fa-4a71-b51a-3e692b1f9665)

Maybe `topFrameWindow` should be called `topSnapshotWindow` instead. after reading through this, my impression is that there's a non-trivial order of execution here, where `snapshotScript` is being executed for all frames in the frame, and they all read each other's `window.__playwright_canvas_render_info__` states. Is this understanding right? By moving this division to the rendering stage, we make an implicit assumption that `window.innerWidth` will be the same at snapshot time and at rendering time. I'm not sure that's true. Do you think we could perform all the heavy lifting at snapshot time instead? That way, we can be more sure that the bounding rect actually refers to the right pixels in the screenshot. I thought of keeping that at snapshot time, but the problem is that most likely we'll hit on XSS issues. I moved those computations to rendering stage because at that point we'll no longer have XSS issues (all rendered frames are under the same domain).

Nevertheless, the end result should be the same, because I capture `window.innerWidth` for each frame and save it in its `__playwright_bounding_rect__` attribute and that's the value I'm using to compute the ratio > Nevertheless, the end result should be the same, because I capture window.innerWidth for each frame and save it in its __playwright_bounding_rect__ attribute.

That makes total sense to me, and resolves my worry about the render-time differences. nice! Yes, you're right. Each parent window, before rendering each iframe, extracts the `__playwright_canvas_render_info__ ` value and keeps in that variable. It then removes the attribute and renders the element normally, which will eventually trigger recursively the same process inside the iframe. Nice, that makes sense. Could you add a comment about that somewhere, for future readers? Also, would `__playwright_frame_bounding_rects__` be a more fitting name? What about this suggestion I gave on https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/33809#discussion_r1868250259 ?

> Maybe topFrameWindow should be called topSnapshotWindow instead. Sounds good as well! What I said was not 100% correct: actually the `window.inner{Width,Height}` is not from iframe's `__playwright_bounding_rect__ `, it was already being captured at snapshot time:

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/d0debf67c0eab87238c51e86e3d9fbc70ca9a260/packages/playwright-core/src/server/trace/recorder/snapshotterInjected.ts#L597-L600

and those are the dimensions I use at rendering time. That's why I changed the `snapshotScript` signature to receive the viewport structure.

Adds `startTime` display to the Call tab.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f103821b-ab4e-43c3-a54a-3231f26d513e)

Adds various time metric display to the Network tab expanded view.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25199fea-365e-4119-83c9-696f0ce8c943)

Minor code cleanup to make it more Reacty.
review_comments:
What's the point in showing these values in the details, given that they are already present in the network table where one can see other network requests and compare their start time/duration? It's a strange omission for it to not be available. Why would expanding the details of something show fewer details?

While you're right that they can only compare when the details are not open, I think it's still valuable to be able to view all the metrics on this screen. While I agree with you that it's nice to see this information in the details view, I still cannot come up with a good explanation why it should be shown above request headers. Maybe push it below headers at least? We should probably put timing information into its own tab and populate it with [other](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-request#request-timing) details that we have, but I don't remember anyone asking for this. It should never happen that `model?.wallTime` is undefined when `activeAction` is not null, why pass `Date.now()` rather than 0 or -1?  Would be cleaner if `CallTab` accepted single parameter `{ action, startTime, startWallTime } | undefined`, can we do that? I don't think `wallTime` is ever null at this line. This is why we need that lint rule :P Doing so requires changing the component significantly so that we properly represent model and `activeAction` as being intertwined state. Currently TypeScript doesn't know they're related.

I would prefer to not change this and leave the coalescence placeholders, but I will change this if you so desire. I personally think this would be overly specific type handling, though it's obviously more correct.
 I don't think "execution" helps here, start time usually applies to execution, maybe name it timeOrigin? This would be just a guess at this point as we can't add ticks to millis, do we really want to explicitly mislead? I would omit. Offline discussion with Yury where I am saying that we should not do wall time math: maybe we could formalize model.startTime and then we can remove the wallTime from individual actions and operate in terms or ticks (monotonic time) for actions only.

This PR fixes the test under `PW_CLOCK=frozen`.

issue_text:
This PR adds a test to ensure we support running UI behind a proxy. It adds websocket support to our vendored `proxy` library as part of that.

Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33705.
Supercedes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/33767, which added the same test but used a separate WS proxy library.

issue_text:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33886. We're concatenating all stdio chunks that are `string`, but we don't concatenate `Buffer` chunks. The addition of `Buffer` attachments seems to go back to https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/26391, but it's not sure if that was a necessary thing.

This PR fixes the issue by encoding all `Buffer` chunks, so they're concatenated together with the rest.

Motivation: This helps us to find out about upstream headless_shell regressions before they appear in the Beta channel.

---

I was considering doing the same pattern like we do for chromium (auto use headless-shell) but this doesn't work here since `chromium-tip-of-tree` is already a channel. Lets keep it how it is and do the manual opt-in.
review_comments: Why can't we just use version of `chromium-tip-of-tree`, we don't expect these two to ever diverge, do we? I'll follow-up.

Without that this Promise ends up in Promise unhandled rejection errors - since we set an error to it (inside FrameSession.dispose) but never read the error.  We wait for it in `FrameSession._initialize` which is called for both main frame and OOPIFs soon after the session is created. I guess there may be an exception before this promise is added to the list of awaited promises, but does it happen in reality? If it does, we probably need to update wkPage too. Can you restructure the code so that `if (pageOrError instanceof Error)` performed just once? Was this not working before because the page may have been an error already? Suppressing errors with .catch(() => {}) might hide important issues. Consider handling the error appropriately or clarifying the intention behind ignoring it.
```suggestion
    this._firstNonInitialNavigationCommittedPromise.catch((error) => { console.error('Error in _firstNonInitialNavigationCommittedPromise:', error); });
``` Maybe do it inside `FrameSession._initialize` and add a comment there that we may get an exception before awaiting the promise? Do you want to use custom browser path and delete ffmpeg from that path?  otherwise I don't understand this test. We have isolated browsers in this test so Playwright does not find any browsers including ffmpeg. I need a browser to start with tho - for that I use Google Chrome. We have other tests relying on Google Chrome as well. added a comment. I think having it close to where the Promise is created is also reasonable. Similar to what we do with `this._stopVideoRecording().catch(() => {});`. done.

issue_text:
The `threshold` option in `perMessageDeflate` is ignored due to context takeover being enabled. This leads to WebSocket RPC messages being unconditionally compressed.

Most RPC channel messages are small, and unconditionally performing message compression has measurable performance impact.

Disable context takeover (for both server and client) to let compression threshold option to take effect.

Fixes #33810
review_comments: I believe (based on [this part](https://github.com/websockets/ws/blob/68614728c164eb55462ff12ba24cb30451d28ec6/lib/sender.js#L372-L375) of the implementation) that `serverNoContextTakeover` doesn't have any effect on the client web socket. If so let's not set it in the options here. Ditto. Let's not set `clientNoContextTakeover` here if it's a noop anyway. Good catch, thanks.

I debugged the issue and I pinned it down to the changes in this pull request. The problem we are having is when we click on a link which triggers the `beforeunload` dialog, after we dismiss the dialog and try to interact with the page again, we get timeout errors. Here is a simple test replicating the error ... ```js const {chromium} = require('playwright'); const {expect} = require('@playwright/test'); (async () => { const browser = await chromium.launch(); const page = await browser.newPage(); await page.mainFrame().goto('https://www.npmjs.com/'); expect(await page.mainFrame().title()).toStrictEqual('npm | Home'); await page.evaluate(() => { window.onbeforeunload = () => false; }); page.on('dialog', async dialog => { await dialog.dismiss(); }); await page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Teams'}).click({noWaitAfter: true}); await page.evaluate(() => { window.onbeforeunload = null; }); // Timeout error will occur here: await page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Teams'}).click({timeout: 1000}); expect(await page.mainFrame().title()).toStrictEqual('npm | Teams'); await browser.close(); })(); ``` The test fails on the line `await page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Teams'}).click({timeout: 1000});` with the error: ``` locator.click: Timeout 1000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for getByRole('menuitem', { name: 'Teams' }) - waiting for navigation to finish... ``` During debugging, I noticed the `pendingDocument()` is set to `{documentId: undefined, request: undefined}` If this line https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/b5bd543cc6935f62732da3b6183bd319eb2bdc2a/packages/playwright-core/src/server/page.ts#L472 is changed to the following, our problem disappears: ```js if (!mainFrame || !mainFrame.pendingDocument() || !mainFrame.pendingDocument().documentId) return; ``` Is this a genuine issue that should be fixed? @chrisbottin This is a genuine issue, I filed #33806 on your behalf. We'll take a look. @dgozman Thanks, I also raised https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33803 after posting my comment here. I've closed it as duplicate now.
issue_text:
This includes all actions that perform locator handler check.
    
Note this makes it impossible to interact with the page while a main frame navigation is ongoing. This was already the case for Chromium, but now WebKit and Firefox align with it.

Setting `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_NAVIGATION_CHECK` environment variable disables this behavior.

issue_text:
There is a race between:
- `Runtime.executionContextsCleared` coming in the OOPIF.
- `Page.frameNavigated`/`Target.attachedToTarget` when frame goes local->remote.

As a result, we can have stale execution contexts from the previous non-OOPIF frame that does not exist anymore, instead of new contexts in the OOPIF.

This causes things like recorder trying to initialize in the wrong context and fail.

Now that we clear contexts upon local->remote switch, recorder waits for the new context to be created an successfully initializes.

issue_text:
Yesterday we found that UI mode is broken on codespaces b/c the new `server` parameter points to `localhost`, which isn't available when the UI is accessed over Codespace's port forwarding host.

This PR fixes that by making the `server` parameter only used in HMR mode. I'm also making the web server connection respect the `server` param in this PR.

I've developed this on a Codespace and verified that it works.
review_comments: `window.location.href` is something like `https://localhost:1234/tracing/uiMode.html`, and this expression turns that into `https://localhost:1234/`. If it was served deeper, like under `https://localhost:1234/azdo-subdir/tracing/uiMode.html`, then it'd turn into `https://localhost:1234/azdo-subdor/`.

Replaces our custom reveal implementation with an abstracted one. `useAnchor` allows subscribing to anchor changes, `<Anchor>` implements `scrollIntoView` behaviour.

review_comments:
Why `export`? Is this supposed to be used without an `Anchor`? I find it strange that the first and only usage is inside `AutoChip`. I'd prefer to separate them for now, and wrap with `Anchor` where needed to separate concerns. Why do we need this logic? If it is collapsed by default, perhaps it's fine for it to be collapsed after scrolling into view? - This `preventDefault` logic is unused. Let's drop it for now?
- Same goes for the `ref` parameter.
- Why would anyone care about `!isRevealed` situation? If anything, I'd call this callback `onReveal()` and call only on reveal. Perhaps only call this when revealed, and rename to `onReveal()`? Is this going to trigger if I click the same "reveal" link again? I'd like the item to be revealed even when it's already in the url. And vice versa, I wouldn't want the item to be revealed on mere re-render, e.g. switching a tab in a tabbed pane. That's the idea, yes. it can be used without UX-Wise, I think uncollapsing on reveal saves one click. This might not make a difference for Traces or Videos. But we'll extend this to a specific attachment in the future, and there's no way of revealing an element in a collapsed Chip. I tried to be cheeky and support every thinkable usecase. But I guess we can remove the unused stuff and add it once needed :) It triggers for each `popstate` event, unrelated of re-rendering. As you can see in the video, this includes clicking the link again. If you have a tabbed pane, and that tabbed pane leads to `popstate` events, then I guess the tabbed pane shouldn't include the `anchor` param in its links. If we want the chip to auto-expand on reveal, then we need to combine them. If not, then i'm happy to separate. Thinking about this one, it means in addition to scrolling into view, we might need to perform other actions to reveal, for example expand the chip.

If we think broadly, the way to solve it would be to add revealing logic to various UI elements:
- Make expandable/switchable elements accept `anchorId` that they will `useAnchor()` with and reveal the respective part of the UI.
- Separate `Anchor` that will scroll into view from the `AutoChip` that will expand, and pass the same `anchorId` to both.
- Make `anchorId` hierarchical in the future, so that we can in theory say "AutoChip that contains all attachments has anchorId=attachments/*", and then inside it put individual "Attachment with anchorId=attachments/0".

Let me know what you think. You've put into words what I couldn't, yes! That's why `useAnchor` is probably gonna be exported in the next PR, and why `anchorId` already accepts a predicate. I'll look at separating the expanding + scrolling logic in AutoChip. I don't think we need `onReveal` anymore, let's drop it.

issue_text:
The trace viewer server has three purposes:

1. serve static assets
2. provide websocket access to test server
3. provide file access

In preparation for hot module replacement, this PR allows specifying a separate backend for 2. and 3.. This could also be helpful in the future in a codespace-like setup.

It adds a `TraceViewerServerBackend` class that encapsulates file access, and propagates the baseURL via a search parameter. It also adds a `/file/` handler to the service worker, so all communication with the trace viewer server is explicitly handled through the service worker.

we know that our server supports range requests, so i'd like to try replacing this with `zipjs.HttpRangeReader` in a follow-up. that should save some memory. - When trace is on the third-party server, we cannot be sure about range requests support.
- Does that mean we'll fetch parts of the zip lazily, only when requested? That sounds both good and bad 😄  Should this one move to `TraceViewerServerBackend` instead? nit: I'd call this just `TraceViewerServer` style: please add empty lines between methods It feels wrong to create this object for each `fetch()`, even though it's stateless. Can we store it next to `client` instead? Not sure what you mean with "storing next to client". Is https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/33542/commits/592f7cc2e33ec145c6e3ee4a72a740562b6f2870 what you have in mind? No, because `TraceViewerServerBackend` is about loading files from disk, and most of this function is not. > When trace is on the third-party server, we cannot be sure about range requests support.

Absolutely, but it should already help if we just do it for our own trace viewer server.

> Does that mean we'll fetch parts of the zip lazily, only when requested? That sounds both good and bad 😄

That's what I hope it means, yes. My hope is that it fetches only the directory upfront, and then uses the range numbers from there to fetch all files lazily. Right now, the `HttpReader` needs to keep the entire zip in memory, even the parts it never reads. I'd rather make it a map from `client.id` to `TraceViewerServer`, and call it `clientIdToTraceViewerServer`, similarly to line 39.

Going even further, I'd put it to the same map as `clientIdToTraceUrls` and make `loadTrace` responsible for creating it. Let me know whether you like it. We don't have `client.id` available for every request (https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/33540 failed tests!), so I don't see how that's possible sadly. I guess we could have a special `TraceViewerServer` that uses the current base URL for the `undefined` client ID. > Going even further, I'd put it to the same map as clientIdToTraceUrls and make loadTrace responsible for creating it. issue_text:
The code for canvas rendering currently assumes that the screenshot it crops from has the same aspect ratio as the frame it's displaying in. That assumption is wrong. The fix is record the canvas position at snapshot time, so that it's relative to the screnshot aspect ratio.
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33562.

Why do we need to test chromium-next on windows and macOS, but not headless-shell? it's technically a new binary as well, are we sure it behaves the same? shouldn't this install chromium-next?

```suggestion
        browsers-to-install: chromium-next

maybe let's also link to issue #x here, for a list of known differences ```suggestion

```

Looks wong? Should we put:

- chromium-next
- download only needed browsers. Saves up to 50s (I think a great one)

In our best practices guide? My understanding is that `chromium-next` has support for extensions even in headless mode. Should this be the condition instead?

```suggestion
  it.skip(headless && channel !== 'chromium-next', 'chromium-headless-shell has no support for extensions');
``` why isn't this test needed anymore? I have manually verified that everything works for the end user. We test `headless-shell` now on every bot, since it's a part of regular `chromium`. This PR gives us hot module replacement for the html report. Enable it with `PW_HMR=1`.

In HMR mode, the HTML report becomes a redirect file to the dev server. We can't pass the ZIP contents via URL, so it's transferred via `postMessage` instead.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d981fd2e-609f-49be-abaa-718f84152a54
review_comments: nit: I'd recommend `filePath` to not hoist the `path` package. Can we guard this by `env.PW_HMR` somehow? I don't want our report to send/respond to random messages from random pages. Sites with `window.playwrightReportBase64` will never reach this call. Do you think that's enough protection?

issue_text:
Fixes #29382

1. The current issue occurs in the `toEqual` call when the `expected` type in `toHaveText` is `(string | RegExp)[]`. Since we cannot modify the external dependency `this.utils.printDiffOrStringify`, normalization is performed before invoking it.
2. As a precaution, I checked the `toMatchText` method, which handles cases where the type is `string | RegExp`, to ensure that regex values are processed correctly. Regression tests confirmed that no issues are present.

issue_text:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/23964.

Trace snapshots are a best-effort snapshots of the browser DOM, but we can't guarantee them to be exactly what the browser showed. One example of this is `canvas` elements, where you just can't see their contents. That makes snapshots useful, but not perfect.

For those cases where the snapshot doesn't show everything, this PR introduces a new setting to show a screenshot instead. You won't be able to scroll or inspect the DOM or select a locator anymore. But if the snapshot was missing something, or displaying something wrong, you can now check the screenshot instead.

Something like `Enable "live snapshots" to pick a locator`? We should make the language consistent though :) Yes that's the idiomatic way, but it has the downside of mounting & unmounting the iframes every time the setting is toggled. By using `display: none`, we keep them in the DOM. This makes all of the above logic continue to work without changes. It should also make toggling between screenshots and snapshots snappier. review_comments:
I moved this block up so it mirrors execution order. this line is the only change though. This breaks the service worker lifecycle, we can't ship it like this. Instead, we can pass the test server port via the trace URL. Shall we remove this now, and a similar property in `vite.config.ts`? Does vite pick up all things in the `public` dir? Note that [docs](https://vite.dev/guide/assets#the-public-directory) say that we must reference public assets through an absolute path - `/sw.bundle.js` in our case. I wonder whether this whole setup works for non-root deployment, e.g. `trace.playwright.dev/next`? Why `*` at the end? What else could this be, except for `sw.bundle.js`? We can't remove this one, because we don't want it to delete the `public` directory. But i've removed the other one, there's no race anymore. https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/33291/commits/29d21fda8d5bd770c172bd1581e0adb166e9f9b8 Yes, it picks up all the things without any processing.

I'm not sure why they say that public assets always need to be resolved through absolute paths. Vite definitely respects the `--base` param when serving `public` assets. I think what they intend to say is that public assets need to be resolved relative to the deployment base path, not relative to the origin root. We're handling all that fine.

> I wonder whether this whole setup works for non-root deployment, e.g. trace.playwright.dev/next?

It does perfectly, just like before. Notice that in L314 of `build.js` we explicitly make it serve under the `/trace/` base path, so we already have a non-root dev environment. it also emits `sw.bundle.js.map`, and I was too lazy to spell that out. but if you're already asking about this, it makes sense to spell it out I guess. will do scratch that - it used to emit the source map in a previous iteration, but doesn't anymore. i've removed the *

issue_text:
Small refactoring leading up to https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/33291. At the moment, when the trace viewer requests a trace file from the service worker, it sometimes passes a file path to the trace viewer, and sometimes a URL to a 3rd party service like dropbox and GH actions. If it's a file path, the service worker will then convert that into a URL on the test server.

This PR changes moves this resolution logic into the trace viewer. It will allow #33291 to easily change the port used for the test server.
review_comments:
A comment would help me understand the shape of the url.

`...&trace=http://localhost:3333/trace/file?path={path/on/file/system}` FetchTraceModelBackend is only used for live mode where traces are always on fs. I don't think changing string to URL here is helpful. Surprised to see file:// here which bypasses the service worker and is different from /trace/file?path= schema I'm seeing in other places. tracePathorURL: URL sounds strange to me! Ah! So that's where you are making a conversion back. Let's stick with /trace/file?path= as a way to point to local files and avoid double conversion. I've changed this so that the `path` parameter is templated on reading, not on write. We won't get around some URL manipulation though, because `traceURL` is now absolute and not relative anymore. Adds a button to attach steps that opens up the Attachment tab and scrolls the selected attachment into view.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5633f55d-2790-4b44-b7d5-c080205ae8f4

I've added a couple of ARIA props to make this easier to test.
review_comments: Perhaps put this to the left of the duration? Misaligned durations look ugly. We usually add a className conditionally, and then put all styles into a css file. Perhaps just `activeAction?.attachments?.includes(attachment)`? - I am not sure you'd like the whole tabpanel to have this title. I'd expect titles on internal elements of the tab content, not a single one covering the whole panel. - I am afraid that `id`s will clash between various tabbed pane. Should we prefix them with some unique value for this `TabbedPane`? tried that, but it doesn't work because referential equality is lost in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/2e01154bb57f5cb34c805092e0119742c46b95d8/packages/trace-viewer/src/ui/attachmentsTab.tsx#L93 addressed: - I guess if there are multiple attachments for the `activeAction`, you probably want to reveal just the first one? - It seems to me that merely selecting a different action will reveal its attachments? Is that the UI we'd like? I'd prefer highlighting them instead, and only reveal upon an explicit button click. Given that this scrolls, the prop should be called `reveal`, leaving `highlight` for visual indication instead. Maybe `ariaControls`? It is very strange to see a property named like this :) You probably want to `React.useCallback()` here to avoid a new function instance every time.

This PR implements #33047 .

It shall be possible to add groups to trace logs so that also users that do not use Playwright-Test, like Playwright Python, Robot Framework, Cucumber etc., can also group their traces.
Similar to test.step visually.

We usually inline all options here, and avoid extra types like `TracingGroupOptions`. That would mean putting `location` right next to `name`. ```suggestion
Creates a new inline group in the trace, causing any subsequent calls to belong to this group, until [`method: Tracing.groupEnd`] is called.
``` ```suggestion
Closes the last opened inline group in the trace.
``` nit: I'd pass `parentId` as a parameter to `createBeforeActionTraceEvent()` instead, to keep objects immutable when possible. I'd reuse the `metadata.id` from the `metadata` that is passed to `TracingDispatcher.tracingGroup()` as a second parameter. That will connect stacks/sources machinery to this trace event automatically. Instead of handling the stack manually, we should fall back to the default machinery. issue_text:
3 modes:

- **pass-through:** We call `ensureOpened` after the server negotiated and set the actual underlying `ws.protocol` setting.
- **mock via protocol as a string:**: There we select the given one.
- **mock via protocol as a string array:**: There we select the first one and pretend this one was negotiated.

Its getting set right before we emit the `open` event. Before its an empty string as per [here](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebSocket/protocol).

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33425.

- I don't quite like IIFE when we don't really need it. Can we do if/else chain instead?
- What about `WebSocket.extensions`? Perhaps we should do the same. 1. Done.
2. `WebSocket.extensions` are getting handled by the browser, hence it looks simpler there. should I add a test for it? It would require to enable deflate conditionally in the WS server in `tests/config/testserver/index.ts:81`. Maybe create a WS server inline?

issue_text:
As.discussed yesterday, this PR follows up on https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32955 with some ordering simplification. The new ordering is:

1. All `globalSetup` entries, in direct order
2. All callbacks returned from `globalSetup`, in reverse order
3. All `globalTeardown` entries, in direct order

Before we added support for multiple global setups, a failing callback meant that we wouldn't execute the teardown. This is broken by this change.
review_comments: I think this is already covered by `globalSetup1` from the previous test, isn't it? it is, yes. and it's also covered from the other test I had to touch. but since this is the main breaking behaviour change, and I wanted to have an explicit test to cover this.

While looking at solving https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/26848 we investigated various ways.

1. We tried serialising error causes as multiple errors which didn't gave us a great DX. (https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32834)
1. We tried modifying the `.stack` property which we don't like since it might break our users. (https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/28488)
1. Exposing a separate `.cause` property felt like the best solution since its not breaking any users. It requires customers now to look at this property and the serialise the error appropriately.

This PR implements option 3.

I tested the experience across the following consumers:

1. UI Mode, looks good.
2. JSON reporter: We use this for testing, so its covered.
3. PWT inside worker process (TestInfoError): Looks good, I test it inside the test.
4. VSCode extension: Requires us to serialise the error there, see https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-vscode/pull/547.

Relates https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/26848

This PR clarifies our docs for custom matchers. If `pass` is true, we know that `message` is only used for negated matches. From Jest's `expect` docs:

> `pass` indicates whether there was a match or not, and `message` provides a function with no arguments that returns an error message in case of failure. Thus, when `pass` is false, message should return the error message for when `expect(x).yourMatcher()` fails. And when `pass` is true, message should return the error message for when `expect(x).not.yourMatcher()` fails.

Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33293

How is thinking about `pass == isNot` better than just passing `isNot` for `isNot`? The behaviour around when `message` is respected confused the user in the issue. They thought that if a matcher passes, then `message` is respected. That's what this clarification is about. Passing static `isNot` makes this behaviour more explicit. Maybe we should also add some docs copy here. I've updated the copy in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/33321/commits/946338d572906e933474d6a64d5eb24a62470ac8, let me know what you think I still prefer a direct `isNot: this.isNot` here. Do not encourage users to do a mental math and compute the value here, it is important that isNot is this.isNot and nothing else. Passing it as is is simpler than pre-computing it for the computer, less error-prone. In our own matchers we use a following pattern:

```js
const matcherOptions = {
  isNot: this.isNot,
  promise: this.promise,
};
```
followed by

```js
matcherHint(this, receiver, matcherName, receiver, expected, matcherOptions)
```

That way we never think about it, no matter which branch of message is computed. ditto Alright, i've reverted it. Do you feel the same about the string templating in line 282?

issue_text:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33146. We were only sending the selector to the main frame, so it didn't reach the `iframe`. The fix is to send it to all frames, and use a heuristic to figure out the intended one.

I placed this heuristic inside the injected script. We could probably also put it inside the server part, not sure which is preferable.

review_comments:
Usually you would create a wrapper function which does it. Then you can just do

```suggestion
  const searchParams = useSearchParams();
```

that's usually more readable  Sounds backwards to me - useContext clearly suggests that the context is used to provide the value. I don't see it recommended https://react.dev/reference/react/useContext, is it common to extract a function that makes a single call?  This seems to be from another PR, revert. It's pretty common to abstract `useContext` away when it becomes somewhat complex. As an example, lots of project have a `useAuth` hook that calls `useContext` internally to get the auth state, but that also implements some helper functions and maybe `useEffect` calls and so on.

In this specific example, I don't see a need for an abstraction. `useContext(SearchParamsContext)` and `useSearchParams()` are equal in readability to me. The moment that multiple callsites use it in similar ways though, an abstraction starts making sense :)

In my case i need to add self signed root certificate to test self-hosed self-signed Firefox sync service ( `ignoreHTTPSErrors` doest not work under this situation , because the request is not from HTML Pages but from Firefox  internally ) +1 to revert request.  Sorry, no client certificates are not what I was looking for. My use case is to add certificates to browser's trust store for server side certificate verification. This can be done via use of [Enterprise Policies feature on Firefox](https://mozilla.github.io/policy-templates/#certificates--install). Commonly used for self signed server side certificates or to test internal (to a particular organization) website whose certificates were issued by a private certificate authority.

issue_text: Came out of https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33146. `frameLocator('iframe')` is synonymous to `locator('iframe').contentFrame()`, but our locator <-> selector processing can't handle `frameLocator('iframe')` well. issue_text: Motivation: We want our users to never use frozen builds, so we try our best to warn them. GitHub Actions has a similar problem, that customers are using outdated GitHub Actions which they deprecate and then people are stuck on old versions. What they are doing is emit a [`warning` message](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/workflow-commands-for-github-actions#setting-a-warning-message), which looks like [this](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/actions/runs/9226701285/job/25450817791). We can do something similar if the user is running on GitHub Actions. This patch is writing a message to the stdout if a `revisionOverride` is getting used. If the customer is on GitHub Actions, a warning message is emitted instead, which gets surfaced on the run summary: Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33205

Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33115.

If we're happy with it, this can supercedes the "show screenshot instead of snapshot" implementation. Will remove that in a separate PR.

This PR adds logic to snapshot rendering that fetches the closest screenshot for the rendered snapshot to clip the canvas contents from it. This is best-effort, and the time alignment won't always be perfect. This is fine if there's no scrolling and the canvas has static contents. We show a warning icon to let the user know about that. Because it's based on viewport screenshots, we don't have data outside of it. Parts of the canvas that aren't available will be shown with a checkered background. Here's a demo:


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e23cb827-a6e5-4817-84e2-fa332f0669af
review_comments:
this test isn't gonna stay, obviously. but you can use it to play around with the feature: `npm run ctest -- --grep 'clipping' --headed`

@dgozman what's the best way of testing this - should we trace a page with a `canvas` and then take a screenshot of the trace, to ensure the screenshot isn't blank? Or somehow compute if it's blank without storing a golden image? I'd prefer this code to live in `SnapshotRenderer` instead. Injecting `swScope` here is unfortunate. Perhaps we should have a relative url for the screenshot, e.g. `/screenshot/<pageOrFrameId>`, and route it through sw main? - Is this going to work nicely for the out-of-viewport canvas? Perhaps we should say "not captured" there instead?
- This code must run after `scrollLeft/scrollTop` are restored in `onLoad()`.
- We should still have a warning somewhere that would explain that image might be wrong. I think that would be a flaky test, unfortunately. Perhaps just check some test-specific logging, like we do in recorder tests:

```js
if (isUnderTest) console.error(`drawn 15;23-184;566 screenshot rect on the canvas`);
``` Please handle `img.onerror` as well. How would `SnapshotRenderer` get access to `screencastFrames`? Would we pass them into `.render()`, or do we pass them into the constructor? I had that in a first iteration, but that requires making sw main listen to not just `swScope`, but also to requests from the `iframe` origin. Would that be fine? Alternatively, we could also use a fake origin like `playwright.sw`. done implemented all of it I've since moved the code a little, but it's still inside the server. Let me know how to proceed. made it work with a new route in the service worker 👍 thanks, good idea! implemented we discussed this offline and ended up with https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/33119/commits/45d1b54226e31615e26bbdb6e47830c4cc665e48. I predict this will be flaky 😄 We usually do a few rafs in the hopes it will redraw, but even that does not always help. There is `isTopFrame` somewhere around already, let's reuse it. It's not really a warning anymore, just a checkerboard. Let's skip both `drawWarningBackground` and `drawImage` calls in this case. What's a raf? I've made it skip `drawImage`, but I don't think we should skip `drawCheckerboard` - having that around is still valuable to show that there's something missing. I've also made it skip `drawCheckerboard` to align with what we discussed in the meeting. Gonna potentially change that in a follow-up. https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/33119/commits/ea4116e64546dca6b41160c50a42c69e86cc3fcd It's [`requestAnimationFrame`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/requestAnimationFrame)! See https://github.com/Skn0tt/playwright/blob/ea4116e64546dca6b41160c50a42c69e86cc3fcd/tests/page/pageTest.ts#L39.

issue_text:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32369

The idea behind ordering is that for pairs of setup/teardown, each pair is only torn down after all pairs executed after it are torn down. This allows "stacking" these setup steps onto another, where one setup depends on the previous setup.

For  `globalSetup: ['s1', 's2'], globalTeardown: ['t1', 't2']`, this results in order `s1, s2 ; t2, t1`.

There's a second API some people use where setup steps return their respective teardown steps. If that API is used exclusively, the same ordering applies. Mixing both APIs is discouraged, as that gives hard-to-reason-about ordering.
review_comments:
I'd remove this test, it does not test an essential part of our test runner.

Instead, it would be great to test what exactly do we run in what order, when there are multiple global setups and teardowns, including teardown functions returned from global setups, and some of them fail. Look at how other tests use `result.outputLines`. I find the proposed behavior reasonable, so not really sure I understand the TODO in the description. I've removed the test in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32955/commits/4316a0178dcf0f70afc700ec1fe8a4ea620f2e73 and and added lots of coverage in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32955/commits/3ef8178cca9b70d4b9df39f4374e663750d8ae91. Also amended the PR description with my thoughts around ordering. Done in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32955/commits/38b7dee4423f24645a1e43e88a4aac3f7217834e I kept this pretty short so we don't overload it. Let me know if you think we need to talk about ordering here. We literally overload it here, which is fine. Not sure the wording of your doc is right though, please revise. nit: there isn't much to take first from, this is pretty much `| null` I don't see why teardowns correspond to setups, I'd say those are independent. I'd also pass array of global setups into all teardowns. I think it's right - what would you recommend instead? Would you prefer this?
```suggestion
      globalSetup: this.globalSetups[0] ?? null,
``` Setup functions can return a teardown function, so these functions need to be passed from the setup phase to the teardown phase. I think it's fair to keep them in one task. Do I understand correctly that you'd prefer to tear apart setup and teardown into individual tasks? You are fine. It felt like a couple of words are missing. "Pass an array of file names to specify multiple global setup files" nit means "while you are here if you also find it weird, replace it". Your suggestion works. I'd like to understand what the semantics here is. Let's say I have a database and an auth token. My database requires setup and teardown, my auth token only requires setup. Would there be a difference between the following configurations:

```js
globalSetup: [dbSetup.ts, authSetup.ts],
globalTeardown: dbTeardown.ts,
```
and

```
globalSetup: [authSetup.ts, dbSetup.ts],
globalTeardown: dbTeardown.ts,
```

This `index` parity confuses me and makes me think there is a difference. The difference is in execution ordering. First executes `dbSetup, authSetup ; dbTeardown`, second executes `authSetup, dbSetup ; dbTeardown`. In your usecase, this probably doesn't make a difference. good idea! added the words in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32955/commits/c8c483cacbfe313bbe2b88283e65c95a065fcbb7. ```suggestion
    // 'globalTeardown1' is missing, because globalSetup1Function errored out.
``` I'd also throw here, and check that it did not prevent globalTeardown1 from running. nit: I think that latest TypeScript understands `script => !!script` and figures out the type automatically. Nice! https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-5-5/#inferred-type-predicates

It can only do `script !== undefined` though apparently, `!!script` didn't work for me. Did that in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32955/commits/a72ec6e8245a1725995400429a4ed26481c7cc9b. This behaviour is surprising to me, was somehow expecting a failing `teardown` to stop further teardowns from being executed.

With that in mind, I don't think that a teardown function returned from `globalSetup` should behave any differently than a `globalTeardown` when it throws an error. I've made sure that a failing function doesn't block any `globalTeardown` script from being executed in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32955/commits/9b785662f6e04f13f183985cf1f3b341e3480db3. Would be lovely if you could give that another look.

I think this could benefit from another refactoring where we pull `globalSetup` and `globalTeardown` scripts into separate tasks, but i'd like to get this PR merged first and then refactor in a follow-up. On a second note, this could be considered a breaking change. If folks are currently relying on the `globalSetup` result throwing an error to prevent `globalTeardown` from being executed, that's broken with https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/commit/9b785662f6e04f13f183985cf1f3b341e3480db3. So maybe we should just stick with the incongruence. I agree, let's not touch the relative behavior of `globalSetup` returned function vs `globalTeardown`. The aim here is to support multiple, and our general rule is that all teardowns run even if one of them fails. This applies to fixtures, afterEach and afterAll hooks, and now to global teardown as well.

issue_text:
### Description

Fixes [issue #30662](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/30662)

This PR adds support for `test.fail.only` in Playwright Test, allowing developers to focus on a specific test that is expected to fail.

>- Implemented the `test.fail.only` method.
>- Added regression tests for `test.fail.only` to ensure correct behavior.
>- Updated documentation and TypeScript definitions (`type.d.ts`) to include `test.fail.only`.

As this is my first contribution, I would appreciate feedback on the regression tests and documentation updates. If there are any changes needed, I'm happy to make them. :)

issue_text:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32951

`node:http` reuses TCP Sockets under the hood. We weren't cleaning up our listeners, leading to the `MaxListenersExceededWarning`.

This PR adds cleanup logic. It also raises the warning threshhold, so that it doesn't trigger until there's 100 concurrent requests over the same socket.

issue_text:
Fixes a bug discovered in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32647. When using http proxy, the `connect` event isn't emitted so we don't populate `tcpConnectionAt`. The updated version of `https-proxy-agent` emits a `proxyConnect` as a replacement, so this PR updates and listens to that event.
For socks proxies, the `on("socket")` event is emitted once the SOCKS connection is established, which is the equivalent of having a TCP connection available.

issue_text:
This is fixing a case where the test failed with strict mode violation, but all the matched elements are not highlighted in the trace. 

For example, all the buttons will be highlighted when the following line fails due to strict mode violation:
```ts
await page.locator('button').click();
```

To achieve this, we mark elements during `querySelector` phase instead of inside `onBeforeInputAction`. This allows us to only mark from inside the `InjectedScript` and remove the other way of marking from inside the `Snapshotter`.

issue_text:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32853

Vite turns the shorthand fragment notation `<></>` into `import { Fragment } from "react"; <Fragment></Fragment>`. On the Node.js side of things, this `react` import resolves to our mock version of React, which currently mocks `Fragment` as `{}`. Currently, we pass that straight to `React.createElement`, which throws an error.

The fix is to make our `Fragment` mock detectable with a tag, and when we render it replace it with the real `__pwReact.Fragment`.

issue_text:
In https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32872, a user notes that we document `.focus()` to not timeout by default, but in practice when used without the test runner, it defaults to a 30s timeout.

I've discussed this with Dima, and he noted that our JS documentation focuses on usage with the Playwright test runner, not with the library. The test runner disables timeouts for operations in favour of timeouts for test cases. In the library, we default to a 30s timeouts. This PR adds this to the "key differences" table.

Its caused by a change made [here](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/commit/11014145ce37a8d44b6083fcf2c5f71453f018c7#diff-10d158206c9e19b9603a57206aa089d4b827dc541b86495a9ce5ca921b8d2f28R82). With that we call `this._fireChange()` twice for the same set of actions. This ends up in two `sourceChanged` events in the debug controller. We should not fire the same 'change' event if its not enabled.

Why was it racy? Because its fired in a microtask, depending on the load, it might or might not happen - turns out it only happened on busy systems.

For Chromium and Firefox we have a single Linux binary which works across all the Ubuntu versions.

For WebKit this is not the case. We have a binary per Ubuntu version.

This allows us to stop spanning the matrix across all the ubuntu versions and only running the headed WebKit tests on older Ubuntu versions.

In other words, this stops testing:

- ubuntu20-chromium
- ubuntu20-firefox
- ubuntu22-chromium
- ubuntu22-firefox

issue_text:
Adjusted whitespace to ensure step details are included in resulting HTML lists items. ## Details Using initial whitespace in Markdown to embed the instructions for a step within that step block rather than being separate, non-list content blocks. As a side benefit, this can make the list easier to consume for users with screen readers. For VoiceOver, for example, there are several superfluous "list start" and "list end" notices. ### Current/Prior HTML Each list item is a new ordered list and code blocks are outside the list structure. ```html
  1. {title}
{code block}
  1. {title}
{code block}
... ``` ### Proposed HTML One ordered list where item code blocks are part of the now-automatically numbered step. ```html

  1. {title}

    {code block}

  2. {title}

    {code block}
    3. ...
```

I did b) in this case, which seems more reasonable.

We run the Trace Viewer in the tests using `launchApp` which uses [`noDefaultViewport: true`](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/33890eb6c5298b239b42763e4652b3c7e40bf68f/packages/playwright-core/src/server/launchApp.ts#L47). The window size on CI is probably just 1024x720 or something like that (assumption).

We could also check for `toBeLessThan`.

issue_text:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32680

Problem: `Location` type is a global in `node_modules/typescript/lib/lib.dom.d.ts`.

Previously we used it only in our reporters (`testReporter.d.ts`) now we also use it inside `test.d.ts`. We don't want to import `testReporter` from `test.d.ts`, hence moving the type into `test.d.ts`.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/30160 ### Description: This pull request introduces the ability to specify custom locations for test steps in Playwright. By enabling the provision of arbitrary locations to the test.step method, it resolves the limitation where helper methods obfuscate the original call site, providing more accurate and meaningful location data in test reports. ### Motivation: To enhance the utility and clarity of test reports in Playwright. Specifically, it addresses the need to trace test steps back to their precise location in the code, which is especially important when steps are abstracted in helper functions. This feature is crucial for maintaining accurate documentation and facilitating debugging processes. ### Changes: Added functionality to pass a custom location object to test.step. ### Expected Outcome: This PR is expected to significantly improve the precision and usefulness of diagnostic data in test reports by allowing specific locations within helper functions to be accurately documented. It facilitates better tracking of test executions and simplifies the debugging process, making it easier for developers to understand and address issues within complex tests. ### References: Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/30160 - "[Feature]: allow to pass arbitrary location to test.step" **Code Check** I conducted tests on this new feature by integrating it into some existing test codes, and it worked well. Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32632. A side effect of Remix's hydration implementation is that it throws away the entire DOM. This is broadly discussed in https://github.com/remix-run/remix/issues/4822 - there might be a fix in coming React versions, but who knows.
Besides breaking browser extensions, this also deletes our toolbar!
This PR fixes it by periodically checking in on `x-pw-glass`, and remounting it if it was unmounted. Hacky but effective!

issue_text:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32578.

Adds a buffer mode that can be toggled by pressing <kbd>b</kbd>. When engaged, changed test files are collected and shown on screen. The test run is then kicked off by pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd>.

This changes the signal to start a test run from <kbd>Cmd+s</kbd> to a <kbd>Enter</kbd> press in the test terminal. It should help users with auto-save and make it easier to run on long-running tests. It feels very similar to running `npx playwright test`, but without having to write a filter.

issue_text: Adds a copy-to-clipboard button for each annotation so that text can be copied easily. This re-uses the existing `CopyToClipboard` component and adds a `small` variant that can be used inline. The icon size and colour have been chosen to avoid being overwhelming when used inline. Add a method to Page that forces garbage collection. For now this method is supported only in Chromium and WebKit.

~I made several attempts to get this to work in Firefox, using both [Components.utils.schedulePreciseGC](https://udn.realityripple.com/docs/Mozilla/Tech/XPCOM/Language_Bindings/Components.utils.schedulePreciseGC) and [Components.utils.forceGC](https://udn.realityripple.com/docs/Mozilla/Tech/XPCOM/Language_Bindings/Components.utils.forceGC), but was unsuccessful. See https://github.com/marmphco/playwright/commit/42bd3ef906b43faacf329432600f3131203b8d1a for those changes. Either garbage collection isn't running or its effects aren't visible immediately to the test code like they are for WebKit and Chromium. I don't have a good enough understanding of Firefox's internals to figure this out so I left it as unsupported for now. If this is unacceptable I can try to implement via a different route. Suggestions for better approaches would be appreciated 🙂~

7c826ee includes support for Firefox.

Closes #32278

We're only running the Vite build if there's a component testing plugin registered, in which case we need to run Vite to get a correct result. In the common case without component testing, `populateDependencies: true` is a no-op. Could you outline a scenario where this adds unnecessary cost? Wait, ignore me - listing tests does *not* need a vite build to return a correct result. Dependency population is what needs the vite build, but one could be interested in listing tests without caring about dependency population. Gonna implement your recommendation. done in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32583/commits/7827ca77c547838385b0eca71cdf52e2dad514d1

review_comments:
I don't think we want to mess up with userland overrides. Can we have any other workaround instead? I restore them after `JSON.stringify` (and my test already checks it) but I suppose there are some corner cases that I'm not thinking of. One option would be to only rely on `JSON.stringify` if none of those types defines `toJSON`, otherwise implement it ourselves. There's probably a simple solution: ensure all properties of `SerializableValue` override `toJSON` as `null` if its prototype defines it. I'll test it today. That's an interesting idea. Did you have a chance to try it out? I just force pushed a new patch. I implemented an alternative to `JSON.stringify` instead because it adding `toJSON` property to objects could lead to side effects.

It is working fine with `Array.prototype.toJSON`.

Primitive types serialization like number or string are not impacted with a custom `toJSON` implementation so I left them out.

I also left out `Object.prototype.toJSON`. If users mess up this function, it will make playwright fail, but I don't think there's much we can do, because it's a fallback mechanism for custom object serializattion:

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/8995ace8253ad25865a04452408967e929911205/packages/playwright-core/src/server/isomorphic/utilityScriptSerializers.ts#L214-L224  I looked at the last commit, and I don't think it's worth it. Manually rolling `JSON.stringify` is non-trivial. For example, your current implementation ignores `toJSON()` for objects and does not handle infinite recursion. I am sure there are more edge cases that built-in implementation covers.

I think it's ok if `exposeBinding` does not work on some sites that mess up with builtins. To be testable, these will have to be updated. Alternatively, one can remove custom `toJSON()` override from `addInitScript()`, as long as the site keeps working.
 Just a note: my implementation is not intended to be generic, it doesn't handle recursion simply because the structure is not infinite recursive (it's an object with `SerializableValue` objects), and regarding custom `toJSON`, they are also already applied at that stage too. But I see your point For the record, we had a similar attempt (in spirit) to make codegen work on sites that mess up with builtins - see #6187. However, we have decided that's too much complexity for too little benefit, and it worked so far. This case seems similar. I agree, sometimes it's not worth it. I would propose a change however: this problem manifests itself as a `serializableArgs.map is not a function`, just like in #22460, from 

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/8995ace8253ad25865a04452408967e929911205/packages/playwright-core/src/server/page.ts#L849

If `serializedArgs` is not an array, it should throw a better error to the end user, so that they know Array.prototype.toJSOn is probably messed up. That sounds good to me, looking forward to the PR. I just pushed a new change, with a more explicit error message.

issue_text:
What was happening?
- When we use CT, we go over the test files, look at the imports using `tsxTransform.ts` and store them inside a map, these we feed into the import registry which we build using Vite and have access inside the browser
- In case of an inline component in the same file as where the test file is, this is not happening.
- jsx-runtime via babel kicks in, transforms every JSX component in something like that:

```
{
  __pw_type: 'jsx',
  type: [Function: MyInlineComponent],
  props: { value: 'Max' },
  key: undefined
}
```

this then gets passed into `wrapObject` which maps any function from the Node.js side into expose function calls so they work inside the browser. The assumption for `wrapObject` was to do it mostly for callbacks. So it does for `type` - which is actually our component. We then pass this to the React render function, which calls back the exposed function but we never return anything, so it mounts `undefined`.

---

While there have been experiments from certain vendors to get the 'client only' code inside a server side file, we should throw for now to not confuse users. We might revisit this in the future since Babel / TSX doesn't support it outside of the box.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32167

issue_text:
In this test, the trace recording goes super fast. Sometimes, this means that the recording is finished before the screen recorder got a chance to take a screenshot. If that happens, the tests fail because we never show a screenshot. 
This PR fixes the flakiness by delaying the trace recording so that there's always a screenshot taken.

issue_text:
In the `visit` method, we currently cache the rendered HTML for every walked node. This re-use works well for traces that consist mostly of references to earlier snapshots.
But for traces that don't share much, this is a large memory overhead and leads to the memory crash documented in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32336. For the algocracks amongst you, the current memory usage for an html tree $h$ is $\mathcal{O}(|h| * \text{height}(h))$.

This PR removes that cache from the nodes and replaces it with a snapshot-level cache, fixing the memory crash.
Traces *without* reference should not see a performance impact from this.
Traces *with* references will have slower initial rendering, but re-rendering maintains speed because of the snapshot-level cache.

Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32336

After API review we decided to revert it:
* VSCode extension and UI mode users already get the (runtime) error if the tag is not prefixed
* The typescript error message is not very nice
* The type change would break those clients that generate tests with tags passed as string

This reverts commit 90e7b9ebacbd597b7380522001eb6d17ee9c3d86.

Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32076.

This PR rewrites `watchMode.ts` to use `TestServer` under the hood. It's essentially a complete rewrite, so don't pay too much attention on the old implementation. Note that there's no changes to tests, so all behaviour we have specced out there still works.

To make this work without a superfluous WebSocket connection, I had to refactor `TestServerConnection` a little. Originally, I pulled this into a [separate PR](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32132), but then realised how small the refactoring is. So it's in this PR now. Let me know if you'd like to land it separately.
review_comments:
this is entirely untested, and ideally i'd like to add a test for it - but i'm not sure how to do it best. I tried writing a demo page that reads from `localStorage` across the two test runs, but that gets cleared. how could we assert that a browser is reused? Let's make this an explicit interface. Note we have some `Transport` interfaces out there, and even a `WebSocketTransport` implementation. I wonder whether we can reuse one, maybe in a follow-up. I'd rather all clients do `new TestServerConnection(new WebSocketTransport(wsURL))` instead of this. As they say, "prefer aggregation over inheritance". Making this sync seems like an unrelated change. Usually, we would not touch it because it does not bring any value but introduces churn when blaming around. WDYT? Please declare `send` and `close` explicitly. I've already lost them when reading this, and wondered for a while how does this implement the socket interface. Why do we want to intercept stdio, when we immediately write it back? I think we should not pass `FullConfigInternal` to this method. Instead, the `TestServer` should load the config, and we should operate on some kind of options, maybe even on `ConfigCLIOverrides`. See how `program.ts` calls `testServer.runUIMode` instead of loading the config. It seems like watch mode and ui mode have different ideas about watch semantics. Let's write them down and figure out whether we want to unify them or maybe update test server to support both, or something else. I'd not worry about testing this piece for now. The big difference I see is that in `--watch`, there's no way of selecting individual parts of the test tree to be watched. I also don't think that'd be ergonomic in the terminal. Are there any other differences that we want to unify? done! good call, removed that. aye aye! 🫡 done good idea! made it explicit for now. @dgozman how would you call this? it's essentially `additionalFileMatcher`, but via the testserverconnection. - UI mode watches a specific list of files, and passes all test files when "Watch All" mode is enabled, while this watch mode does not "watch" any files.
- UI mode does not run dependencies upon a watched test run, while this mode does.
- This mode applies filters like grep after being notified about changed files, while UI mode applies filters before passing the list of files to watch (IIUC).
 Let's make `onlyChanged`-related changes in a separate PR? IIUC, we do not support `onlyChanged` in UI mode as well? We seems to push into this array over and over again, on each test run, don't we? I think we should not need this if we align with UI mode. Happy to move it into a different PR if you want. The reason I included it here is that we supported onlyChanged in the previous impl of watch mode, and had a test for it: https://github.com/Skn0tt/playwright/blob/e8ad5cac6f9071293297287053c4c5313c65b1d2/tests/playwright-test/only-changed.spec.ts#L169 We do! We could either clear it on every new test run, or make it a `Set`. I've turned it into a `Set` in 05ea3955564ef4f46b9a2d3c6f100b465fc867e9. - In the current implementation, I don't see the UI calling `watch` at all. It calls `initialize` once with `watchTestDirs: true`, but apart from that it never changes the list of watched files. I made this implementation do the same in c6d72fe2a1e061acdfee64a59eea9c61d3b4208b.

- UI mode does run dependencies, see 184b2b03eb4c7e02d52824546efa39b2cdbf6784 for a test that proves that.

- UI mode applies the filters after being notified as well. It does that in https://github.com/Skn0tt/playwright/blob/184b2b03eb4c7e02d52824546efa39b2cdbf6784/packages/trace-viewer/src/ui/uiModeView.tsx#L352-L374.


 If we align with UI mode's way of passing an exhaustive list of test IDs, then we wouldn't need it. In order to do so, it needs to walk the entire test tree though. That's complex. It's fine in the UI, because it allows watching only select tests. We don't need that functionality in CLI watch mode though.

We still need something to filter down the test run to dirty files, and this `files` property is an easy-to-understand way of doing that. We should move this further up, similar to the line 164, without loading the config at all, and without involving `Runner`. Note: we do not ever emit `error` events, because failing to handle them makes Node exit. Rename the event to something else, e.g. `transportError`. This one is not supported now. nit: `teleSuiteUpdater`? I think it is now easier to pass `testId` filter instead, given that you have `teleSuiteUpdater.rootSuite.allTests()`.

Bumps [micromatch](https://github.com/micromatch/micromatch) from 4.0.5 to 4.0.8.
Release notes

Sourced from micromatch's releases.

4.0.8

Ultimate release that fixes both CVE-2024-4067 and CVE-2024-4068. We consider the issues low-priority, so even if you see automated scanners saying otherwise, don't be scared.

Changelog

Sourced from micromatch's changelog.

[4.0.8] - 2024-08-22

  • backported CVE-2024-4067 fix (from v4.0.6) over to 4.x branch

[4.0.7] - 2024-05-22

  • this is basically v4.0.5, with some README updates
  • it is vulnerable to CVE-2024-4067
  • Updated braces to v3.0.3 to avoid CVE-2024-4068
  • does NOT break API compatibility

[4.0.6] - 2024-05-21

  • Added hasBraces to check if a pattern contains braces.
  • Fixes CVE-2024-4067
  • BREAKS API COMPATIBILITY
  • Should be labeled as a major release, but it's not.

issue_text:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32256

We were expecting all errors to be of type `ExpectError`, but apparently `expect` propagates rejections in the polling functions right through. So we also need to handle that case.

I wonder if we have more cases of this. Would it make sense to enable `useUnknownInCatchVariables` in TypeScript?
review_comments: Why wrapping into `Error(...)`? I'd think the next line is sufficient. style: we only use `_leadingUnderscore` for private fields, not for local variable. done in e4b1dc95dc5155dfbad915358cda5b09f89d4c7d Because both `step.complete()` and `testInfo._failWithError` require the `Error` type and don't take `unknown`. Actually, both of these are ready for non-`Error` errors, but the types are incorrect. I think we should add a test for this just in case, similar to the one in this PR. Done in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32257/commits/e4b1dc95dc5155dfbad915358cda5b09f89d4c7d. The test in this PR already has the non-`Error` case. Let's add a second test that would have the predicate `async () => { throw 'String value'; }`. done in 6b07b2287b2bea98fbfdba1a0611952183393827

issue_text:
Investigation: Currently when a TLS handshake error happens on a http2 connection, the response gets corrupted. This is because:

1. The client (browser, internalTLS) sends a http2 handshake to our proxy
1. The target connection emits a `secureConnect` event
1. We attach listeners since we received secureConnect event and send the buffered "client hello" data over
1. The target connection emits an `error` event
1. We try to send a http2 response over but the client (browser) already received some parts of the handshake and is confused. This ends up in `Error: Received bad client magic byte string` and `net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR`.

This brought up that using the [`session` event](https://nodejs.org/api/tls.html#event-session) seems to be the right one for our use-case.

Relates https://github.com/playwright-community/playwright-go/pull/480
Example error: https://github.com/playwright-community/playwright-go/actions/runs/10465991368/job/28982096640?pr=480#step:6:166

This allows any time slot that has a legitimate timeout of zero to be updated later on. See test for an example.

Previously, setting timeout to zero at any moment was considered a "debug mode" and any subsequent timeouts were ignored.

issue_text:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32070. We were applying `additionalFileMatcher` not just to `filteredProjectSuites`, but also to `projectSuites`. `projectSuites` is where we take dependency projects from, though - so `--only-changed` led to empty dependency projects, resulting in the reported bug.
    
The fix is to only apply `additionalFileMatcher` on `filteredProjectSuites`.

issue_text:
Certain https servers like Microsoft IIS aka. TLS servers do the TLS renegotiation after the TLS handshake. This ends up in two `'secureConnect'` events due to an upstream Node.js bug: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/54362

Drive-by: Move other listeners like `'close'` / `'end'` to `once()` as well.

Relates https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32004

issue_text:
Resolves https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/28863

I allowed passing `URLSearchParams` and `string` as query params to `APIRequestContext` methods.

Currently, it is impossible to pass duplicated params (which is quite common) using an object because keys cannot be duplicated - e.g. `{ status:  'available', status: 'pending' }`.
Support for `URLSearchParams` and `string` should offer more flexibility in more complex situations.

Let me know what you think.

issue_text:
Value stored in settings doesn't always match the `currentTheme` value. In `applyTheme`:

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/9b3e0e5667ab52b5b750b732a9ec6367602dc5df/packages/web/src/theme.ts#L32-L35

it can set theme to `dark-mode` even if the setting is set to `light-mode` when `prefersDarkScheme.matches` is true, and the setting value is not updated. So, when toggling theme, if it looks into the setting value, it will not change the theme.

This PR replaces the setting with `currentTheme` on `toggleTheme` to compute the right theme to toggle from.

issue_text:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32070. We were applying `additionalFileMatcher` not just to `filteredProjectSuites`, but also to `projectSuites`.  `projectSuites` is where we take dependency projects from, though - so `--only-changed` led to empty dependency projects, resulting in the reported bug.

The fix is to only apply `additionalFileMatcher` on `filteredProjectSuites`.

issue_text:
Supercedes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/31915, closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/31811.

When TypeScript resolves a specifier via path mapping, it does not interpret `package.json`. If path mapping resolves to a directory, it only looks at the `index.js` file in that directory if it's in CommonJS mode.

We need to mirror this in our `esmLoader.ts`.
review_comments:
It seems like TypeScript:
- does not honor `exports` field from `package.json` after the type mapping;
- does honor the default `index.js` and `main` field from `package.json` after the type mapping as explained here: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/modules/reference.html#directory-modules-index-file-resolution. Note that both `index.js` and `main` are ignored for ESM, as explained here: https://nodejs.org/dist/latest-v20.x/docs/api/modules.html#folders-as-modules.

The docs above match my manual testing as well. I think we should follow TS and implement the same logic.

 I've added a test to ensure we follow your first observation in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32078/commits/9a80386c7d057027499609aa4d648549482474fa.

For the second one, isn't that exactly the behaviour we have right now? If there's a `package.json` file, then we let Node.js deal with resolving to either `index.js` or `main`, depending on the ESM mode. - For the `exports` field, it looks like the code will defer to Node.js (when not in ESM), and Node will honor the `exports`. Is that not the case?
- For the `main` field, TypeScript also checks various extensions (e.g. `ts`) after following it, and we currently do not, because we leave it to Node.js. That's a minor thing, but it would be ideal to mirror TypeScript there as well.
- Updating comments to explain these things would be great as well! 1. I believe the test https://github.com/Skn0tt/playwright/blob/9a80386c7d057027499609aa4d648549482474fa/tests/playwright-test/resolver.spec.ts#L609-L644 asserts just that behaviour. Maybe i'm looking at it wrong though.
2. The `.ts` extension is covered by https://github.com/Skn0tt/playwright/blob/9a80386c7d057027499609aa4d648549482474fa/tests/playwright-test/resolver.spec.ts#L572-L607. What other extensions should we cover?

Both of these are about the path mapping case. Are you referring to the case where there's no path mapping?

In https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32078/commits/62ff3fd736429eb9f3e4038694e4d192944489f8, i've added a test to ensure that `main` is ignored in ESM mode, and updated the comments. Yep, the tests look like they cover all the cases. I guess for the item 1, Node.js does not look at `exports` either, which works for us. Thank you for following through!

Oh no, unanticipated failures! I think they come from a subtle change in when state changes are applied in Concurrent React. Before, each `setState` led to its own individual rerender and execution of `useMemo`. Now, the `setState` calls are batched together differently. This means that these two state changes now result in a single state change, rather than two: https://github.com/Skn0tt/playwright/blob/3711474682e7492fc85264922224aa75cf4355a1/packages/trace-viewer/src/ui/uiModeView.tsx#L322-L323 This has the unfortunate side effect that now, the render where we get a finished `testModel`, we also get an undefined `runningState`, so the selection isn't executed anymore: https://github.com/Skn0tt/playwright/blob/3711474682e7492fc85264922224aa75cf4355a1/packages/trace-viewer/src/ui/uiModeTestListView.tsx#L70-L71 Before the React 18 update, we got lucky that this worked. Apparently now they slightly changed their rendering so that it doesn't anymore. A hacky fix would be to put the second `setState` into a `setTimeout`, but i'll try to find a nicer solution. Turns out that React 18 didn't introduce the bug, it just makes it happen more often! I added a fix in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32079/commits/785293fac8ad8b6b79a8e8a9de2d77d979bd7522. It made a test fail that incorrectly asserted the that the UI does not select the failed test, which is not the intended behaviour. https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32079/commits/e4f4dfc4096452d8126d10fccf579ec7d832a691 updates that assertion. ### [Test results](https://mspwblobreport.z1.web.core.windows.net/run-10317510334-1-236a8ac2ac00fe90701bdc3d6c36e840033c5a8e/index.html#?q=s%3Afailed%20s%3Aflaky) for "tests 1"

review_comments:
this closes over `log` from the outer scope, at the point in time where the closure is created. If `log` changes, e.g. because `setLog` is called, this will only be picked up if the component rerenders and the callback is reset. Before Concurrent React, apparently this component was rerendered often enough. With Concurrent mode that doesn't work anymore, though, and `log` sometimes points to an old version of the logs, dropping updates that were applied in between renders :/

The fix is to use an updater function so we always update based on the current version of the state, no matter when `Main` is rerendered.

Docs on updater function: https://react.dev/reference/react/useState#updating-state-based-on-the-previous-state Thanks for the great description!

Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/32050

When keyboarding through the action view, the UI continues showing the hovered action. This makes keyboard nav hard to use.

issue_text:
Pulled out from https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/31900

I stumbled over `React.Children`, because it's the first time I saw that used. https://react.dev/reference/react/Children lists `React.Children` it as "Legacy" and mentions it's uncommon. Also, the fact that SplitView only displays its first two children, and all others are silently discarded, can be a surprise to some.

By separating things out into `sidebar` and `main`, not only do we give the two elements names (otherwise one needs to remember that sidebar is always the first child), but we also prevent any "third children" from being dropped.

issue_text:
Motivation: For scenarios where [`findChromiumChannel`](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/f17de8222fe48e4627983d4f2386deabb00bded2/packages/playwright-core/src/server/registry/index.ts#L1016) throws (no branded browser and no normal browser is installed) we were [silently catching](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/f17de8222fe48e4627983d4f2386deabb00bded2/packages/playwright-core/src/server/recorder.ts#L79) when calling `page.pause()`.

This patch does not invoke `findChromiumChannel` when the inspectedContext is Chromium based and has an `executablePath` specified.

Note this was already fixed by #6214, but regressed since then.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/31967

issue_text:
We populate `localStorage` using an init script. Currently, this script isn't just run for the UI though, but also for all iframes. So we're resetting `localStorage` every time the UI loads an iframe.

This hasn't been a problem in the past, because the only consumer of `localStorage`, `Settings`, only read from `localStorage` once and kept most state in `useState` afterwards. With https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/31911, this is no longer true, so the bug starts biting us!

The fix is to ensure the init script isn't run on iframes.
