issue_text:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/22211

Currently, when the server notifies the UI about changed files, the UI determines what files to re-run based on an old test list. By listing tests before that, we make sure that the test list is up-to-date, and that added tests are included in the next run.

I've also removed the `listChanged` event as discussed in the team sync. The event isn't used anywhere and fires in exactly the same cases where `testFilesChanged` fired, so i've folded them into one another.
review_comments:
Let's update the comment, this is list update + watch now. Or just remove it. Let's comment that we first update the list to get the up-to-date list of tests, and then run the watched ones. Perhaps return if `params.testFiles` is empty? It is unfortunate that we have to create a new `TestTree` here, even though one would be created naturally through `useMemo()`. I wonder whether there is a better pattern to handle such a thing in React? We should double check that emitting `testFilesChanged` event with an empty list of test files is properly ignored in the VSCode extension. You probably want to import from `lib`, not `src`, otherwise path mapping goes crazy. Are we trying to test that there is a single event here? issue_text:
Motivation: When using client-certificates on a website on port `443`, we would normalise the user input with `new URL` but still generate a "bad" representation of the "origin" internally, since the just do concatenated "host:port".

(The origin doesn't contain the port in case of :443)

We use `clientCertificatesToTLSOptions` in two places:

a) for APIRequestContext, there we pass one from the URL constructor over and
b) from the socks proxy, there we **now** also pass a "good one" over.

Test plan: We don't want to run the tests on port :443, so only manually validated the fix.

Relates https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/31906

issue_text:
Motivation: When using `context.request` the `fetch()` call should still use the native TLS options rather than going the proxy route. Before this patch, it used the `defaultOptions` which contain the socksProxy in the `proxy` options and it re-used this. this emitted a warning when visiting `127.0.0.1`, probably due to an upstream bug:

    (node:13882) [DEP0123] DeprecationWarning: Setting the TLS ServerName to an IP address is not permitted by RFC 6066. This will be ignored in a future version.

Probably a regression of https://github.com/TooTallNate/proxy-agents/issues/308.

So based on this it seems fine to ignore the given proxy settings in fetch, if clientCertificates are given. (We would error before when creating the browser context that both is not supported.)

The test changes are needed in order to trigger this warning, which does not get emitted anymore.

```suggestion
Playwright now allows to supply client-side certificates, so that server can verify them, as specified by TLS Client Authentication.

TLS Client Authentication is a web security measure where clients authenticate themselves to the server using a client certificate.
This release adds support for client certificates in Playwright tests.

The fact that the server "requests the client certificate" is an implementation detail that the changelog audience doesn't care about. I've added the fact that this is about web security so it's easier for folks to understand, who have never heard about "TLS" before.

Also, you're talking about `APIRequestContext` here, but also about a browser context below? I'm assuming this works for both, so i've removed the mention. ```suggestion

```

issue_text:
Looking at the last 5 runs on the flakiness dashboard, it shows that Chromium based browsers on Windows are red on this test. This is because on windows 'auxclick' fires before 'contextmenu' (this was also reproduced on a minimal example) which causes an action to be in progress, so when the actual 'contextmenu' fires, it does not emit any actions.

In order to fix it, we ignore right click 'auxclick' events, which sound reasonable, since they are handled via 'contextmenu' event.

I'll open an issue about that. compiling the `className` string like this screams for https://www.npmjs.com/package/clsx to make it more readable. It's just a couple lines of code, we could steal the implementation if we don't want to add a new dependency. What do you think? ```suggestion
        setRunWorkers(value ? '1' : queryParams.workers);
```

Wouldn't this work as well? And then `runWorkers` would be the source of truth instead of always having also check `queryParams.workers`. if we end up needing this more often, this should probably be abstracted into a `ToolbarSection` component. If we had an abstracted `ToolbarSection`, this part would probably be passed as a child to it. That'd make the nesting a little easier to understand on this ```suggestion
  const [, , showRouteActionsSettingInternal] = useSetting(showRouteActionsSetting ? undefined : 'show-route-actions', true, 'Show route actions');
```

The type allows passing `undefined`, so let's use that. This is all very hard to understand. Would it be easier, if you made the `showRouteActionsSetting` prop required, and always passed it down from every parent component? That'd mean that the `useSetting('show-route-actions', ...)` call is duplicated across multiple components, but it'd make the control flow easier to understand. This was my initial implementation. It does not work when you start with `--ui --workers=1`, because the result always evaluates to `'1'`. I agree. I tried that first, but it turned out to be mouthful and not really convenient, because then it's actually two different props - `showRouteActionsSetting` and `showSettings`. I wonder whether there are some best practices for this. Also open for any other ideas on improving this. Yeah, writing an utility function for this and mass-replacing in the source sounds like a nice cleanup. Consider the following snippet:

```
npx playwright test --shard=2/3
npx playwright test --shard=2/3 --last-failed
```

The expectation is that the second invocation runs failed tests from the second shard. To achieve this, we must apply `--last-failed` filter after sharding.

References #33804.
